page: Amazon Web Services r7a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processors. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical CPU cores clocked at 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It integrates 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering 8 GB of RAM per core. The platform includes 38 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. It does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on attached network storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark assessments place this instance in the top decile for multi-threaded compute and in-memory operations. In PassMark and Geekbench multi-core evaluations, the 96 dedicated cores generate top-tier throughput, complemented by strong results in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrate uncached large-block read bandwidth of 327.69 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 154.88 GB/sec. For transactional memory operations, Redis SET benchmarks register 167.91 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression fall within average percentiles, indicating that performance is optimized around aggregate multi-threaded execution rather than single-core frequency scaling.

In terms of resource efficiency, the r7a.24xlarge balances high memory capacity with dedicated core density on AMD hardware. Because all 96 vCPUs map directly to dedicated physical cores, workloads avoid hyperthreaded execution stalls. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage represents an architectural tradeoff for operations requiring high-speed scratch disks, which must be provisioned via remote block volumes. This profile is engineered for memory-bound workloads, including Redis clusters, relational database management systems, big data processing pipelines, and multi-core software build systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on an x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 dedicated physical cores running at up to 3.7 GHz without multithreading, alongside 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. This provides an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio tailored for data-dense workloads. The hardware profile includes AVX-512 vector extensions and 38 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero local storage provided and no discrete GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU benchmarks, Redis key-value operations reaching 167.91 million operations per second, and large-scale software compilation. Given its combination of memory density and sustained multi-core performance, r7a.24xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, high-throughput caching tiers, extensive data analytics, and large-scale batch processing where shared system memory and dedicated execution pipelines are required.
